sources.entry: Homebridge | HomeKit support for the impatient

summary.one_liner: Homebridge is a lightweight Node.js server that runs on your home network to emulate the HomeKit Accessory Protocol and, from v2, expose devices over Matter, so non-HomeKit smart devices can be controlled from Apple Home, Siri, and other controllers.
summary.what_it_does: Homebridge runs as a Node.js server on a home network and emulates the HomeKit Accessory Protocol (HAP). Community-written plugins, published to npm under the keyword homebridge-plugin, bridge HomeKit to third-party smart home device APIs. From v2, plugins can also expose accessories over Matter through the matter.js library, opt-in per bridge via a matter config block. Supported Matter device types include lights, switches and outlets, various sensors, door locks, thermostats, fans, window coverings, robotic vacuums, water valves and generic switches. The README also describes adding bridges to the Home app by scanning a QR code, child bridges for plugins, and a plugin development workflow using npm link and homebridge -D.
use_cases: Control non-HomeKit smart devices from the Apple Home app
Ask Siri to operate devices without native HomeKit support
Expose smart home devices to Matter controllers like Google Home or Alexa
Run a HomeKit bridge on a Raspberry Pi, Linux, macOS, or NAS
Develop and test a Homebridge platform plugin locally
Split plugins into child bridges to get past the 150-accessory limit
how_to_run: Install Homebridge on your platform using the guides linked in the README (Raspberry Pi, Linux, macOS, Windows, Docker, Synology DSM, or other)
Open the Home app, tap Add Accessory, and scan the QR code shown in the Homebridge UI or logs
For plugin development: run npm link inside the plugin folder
Start Homebridge in debug mode with: homebridge -D
Optionally use a separate config folder: homebridge -D -U ~/.homebridge-dev
notable: Plugin ecosystem discoverable on npm via the homebridge-plugin keyword
Matter support is opt-in per bridge and runs alongside HomeKit via multi-admin
Child bridge option lets plugins run separately to avoid the per-bridge accessory limit
Siri and Home app control of devices that have no HomeKit support
caveats: One bridge is limited to 150 accessories due to a HomeKit limit; child bridges or multiple instances work around it
Matter support is not certified by the Connectivity Standards Alliance, so some controllers may show pairing warnings or restrict features
Matter pairing requires the controller and Homebridge on the same IP subnet with mDNS/IPv6 working
A Matter-enabled bridge cannot be moved between controllers without re-commissioning
